html:
The NWT Métis Nation represents the Métis of the South Slave region of the Northwest Territories in Canada, in communities such as Fort Smith, Hay River and Fort Resolution, south of Great Slave Lake. On this map its area stands for their homeland.

The Métis of the north descend from the unions of fur traders, often French Canadian or Scottish men of the North West Company and the Hudson's Bay Company, with Dene and Cree women. They worked as boatmen, guides, hunters and interpreters on the river routes of the fur trade.

When Treaty 8 was signed in 1899 and 1900, many Métis received scrip, a certificate for land or money, instead of treaty rights. In the 2010s they reached a land and resources agreement in principle with the governments. Neighbours: Akaitcho Dene and Métis.
